# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # Every repository VARIABLE, as one static line (#1492). Unlike the secrets
          # below this never changes: `vars` is the context GitHub's own docs define as
          # non-sensitive and render unmasked in logs, so serialising it is not the
          # exfiltration shape that gets a workflow held for approval (#1336) — and this
          # file is the one path a converge cannot write, so keeping it independent of
          # what any task declares is worth a great deal. vars-bag.mjs is the reader.
          CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
          #
          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs

  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs

# The LIVE CANARY (#593 phase 3) — the required final step of any core change.
#
# The fixture rehearsal (vendoring/rehearsal/) is the fast gate: hermetic,
# seconds, on every PR. It has one honest weakness — a fixture only tests what
# someone remembered to model. This is the other half: a REAL repo, really
# adopting Claudinite, really running its own scheduler, converged against this
# canon ref and asked whether it still works.
#
# WHY IT IS A SEPARATE WORKFLOW. It takes minutes, needs a cross-repo token, and
# mutates another repository's working tree. A gate with those properties cannot
# run on every push without becoming something people route around. So: manual
# dispatch, plus automatic on merge to main — the post-merge smoke test, which
# the owner's own framing settles as "still much much better than not knowing".
#
# WHERE THE CANARY IS NAMED. In `.claudinite-settings.json`, on the `local/claudinite`
# pack entry's `config.canaryRepo` — the same tracked pack-entry config mechanism
# the claudinite-fleet-sheepdog pack uses for its fleet scope. NOT a GitHub repository variable: the
# binding between this canon and its canary is a fact about the project, and a
# repository variable is invisible in the tree, absent from every diff, and cannot
# be reviewed alongside the workflow that acts on it. A reader of this repo should
# be able to see which repo CI is about to rewrite.
#
# WHY A DEDICATED REPO, NOT A REAL PROJECT. A rehearsal rewrites the mount and
# can leave a failed converge behind. Pointing that at EdFringeNow means a bad
# canon commit leaves a real project dirty at the exact moment attention is
# elsewhere. The canary is disposable by construction; that is its whole value.
#
# WHAT PROTECTS THE CANARY ITSELF: the worker's rehearsal mode
# (CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF) converges, reports, and then RESTORES the working tree —
# no commit, no branch, no PR, and above all no stamp. Stamping a branch head
# would leave the canary `ref-not-on-trunk`, which vendoring's #328 anti-rewind
# guard then refuses to converge over: a rehearsal that wedges its own canary.
name: Canary rehearsal

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: "Canon ref to rehearse (blank = this workflow's own ref)"
        required: false
        type: string
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Only the surfaces a consumer actually vendors. A README or a doc change
    # cannot break a member, and spending minutes proving that teaches everyone
    # to ignore the result.
    paths:
      - 'engine/**'
      - 'packs/**'
      - 'vendoring/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

# The rehearse step pipes into tee, and GitHub's implicit `bash -e` has no
# pipefail — a worker exiting non-zero into a successful tee would show green.
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

concurrency:
  # One canary at a time: two rehearsals converging the same repo would race on
  # its working tree and report each other's damage.
  group: canary-rehearsal
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  rehearse:
    name: Rehearse against the canary repo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out the canon (for the declaration)
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Resolve the canary repo from the declaration
        id: cfg
        run: |
          CANARY=$(node -e '
            const c = require("./.claudinite-settings.json");
            const e = (c.packs || []).find((p) => p && p.id === "local/claudinite");
            process.stdout.write(e?.config?.canaryRepo ?? "");
          ')
          if [ -z "$CANARY" ]; then
            echo "::warning::No canary declared — skipping the live canary."
            echo "Add config.canaryRepo to the local/claudinite pack entry in"
            echo ".claudinite-settings.json, naming a disposable repo that has adopted"
            echo "Claudinite. Until then the fixture rehearsal is the only consumer gate."
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "Canary: $CANARY (from .claudinite-settings.json)"
            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "repo=$CANARY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Check out the canary
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          repository: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.repo }}
          token: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          path: canary

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # WHICH WORKER RUNS, and why it changed (#768 Phase 5). This drove the CANARY'S
      # OWN vendored worker on the argument that it is the copy a member would run.
      # That argument breaks on the case the gate exists for: the worker is itself
      # vendored content, so a change TO the worker cannot be rehearsed by the copy
      # that predates it — the member's vendored copy is by definition one release
      # behind, and a release is exactly what this is qualifying. So the worker under
      # test is the one THIS REF SHIPS, run against the canary's real tree; it is the
      # code every member will run the moment this release reaches them.
      #
      # The old path is also what made this gate VACUOUS for weeks: the canary flipped
      # to the update mechanism, the baselining worker this step pointed at correctly
      # stood down, and the step passed in zero seconds having converged nothing.
      # Hence the marker check below — a rehearsal that does not say it converged is
      # not a pass, whatever its exit code.
      - name: Rehearse
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
        env:
          CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF: ${{ inputs.ref || github.ref_name }}
          CLAUDINITE_REPO_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/canary
          CLAUDINITE_REPO: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.repo }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        working-directory: packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update
        run: node worker.mjs | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/rehearsal.log"

      # A green step is not evidence; the marker is. Without this, every way of
      # exiting 0 without converging — a stand-down, an early return, a worker whose
      # path moved again — reads exactly like a qualified release.
      - name: Assert the rehearsal actually converged
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
        run: |
          if ! grep -q 'claudinite-rehearsal: converged' "$RUNNER_TEMP/rehearsal.log"; then
            echo "::error::The rehearsal exited 0 without converging the canary — it printed no"

content.content:
# Engine releases

The engine ships as a **version**, not a stream of commits: `ENGINE_VERSION` in
[`version.mjs`](version.mjs) is what a member's stamp records, what an engine
migration's range is written against, and what a pack's `minEngineVersion` is
checked against (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` §2). This file is the log of
those versions and the evidence behind each.

The version is date-anchored `<day>.<n>` — `60820.1` for the first release cut on
2026-08-20. [`version.mjs`](version.mjs) states the shape and computes the next
one (`nextVersion`); rows 1 to 6 below predate the format and are the plain
counter it replaced.

## What a release is

**A release is the commit that bumps `ENGINE_VERSION`, and a bump is only
legitimate once the live canary rehearsal has passed against the tree being
released** (owner decision, 2026-08-12). There is no tag and no separate release
artifact: the updater clones `main` at its newest bumped ref, so the version lives
in the file the mount already carries and there is nothing to cut, push or forget.

The canary is what makes the snapshot *qualified*. It converges a real adopting
repo — running **its own** vendored worker, the copy a member would run — against
the ref under test, and asks whether that repo still works. The fixture rehearsal
on every PR only tests what someone remembered to model; this is the other half.

## Releasing

1. Have the change ready on its branch, CI green.
2. Dispatch **Canary rehearsal** with `ref` = your branch
   (`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml` → Run workflow), and wait for it.
   A red canary is not a release — fix the branch and rehearse again.
3. In the same change: set `ENGINE_VERSION` to `nextVersion` of the one standing
   — a new day restarts the running number at 1 — and add a row below for the new
   version linking the run that passed.
4. Merge. The version now on `main` is the release.

`engine-release-record` (the canon's own local pack) refuses a bump that arrives
without its row, or with a row citing no run — the canary runs in another
repository, so its run id is the only durable evidence the release was rehearsed,
and every member in the fleet is stamped with the number it qualified.

A change that touches the engine **without** bumping the version is an ordinary
engine edit and needs none of this; members receive it on their next converge as
they always have. The bump is what says "this snapshot has been qualified" — so
bump when a migration needs a version to range against, or when a release is
worth naming, not on every merge.

## The log

| Version | Date | Canary rehearsal | What it released |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-08-12 | [run 31628529342](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31628529342) | The first numbered engine: version scaffolding, the versioned stamp, and migration records re-homed under their owning flow (#769). |
| 2 | 2026-08-12 | [run 31633584458](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31633584458) | Migration records gain regex rewrites and the `normalizeLocalDeclarations` codemod, and `local-pack-namespace` starts rewriting local-pack declarations to `local/<id>` — the first release whose records actually change a member's own files. |
| 3 | 2026-08-13 | [run 31655440833](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31655440833) | Baselining retired (#768 Phase 5): the task, its escalation codes and the `migrations/` compatibility entry points are gone, the `agentic:` migration field is rejected rather than ignored, and `updates` becomes the default mechanism. Freshness is measured by version rather than by the age of a ref the update flows never write. |
| 4 | 2026-08-14 | [run 31826589868](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31826589868) | A `needs-human` dispatch issue no longer stops its task (#821): the scheduler's guard suppresses on a live claim rather than on any open issue, so an escalation awaits triage instead of shutting the lane until a person closes it by hand. Bounded — a second unresolved escalation holds the lane, under a verdict of its own that leads the run summary. |
| 5 | 2026-08-19 | [run 32267881121](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32267881121) | The pack renames (#1022): `core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`, `grow_with_claudinite` → `claudinite-growth`, and the scheduled-task authoring contract moved between them. | 6 | 2026-08-19 | [run 32270294377](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32270294377) | The declaration half of the pack renames (#1041). Replaced by a structural op (`applyPackRenames`) driven by the engine's own rename map. A separate record because a repo already stamped 5 never runs the 5 record again — and a converged member is exactly the one whose declaration still needs moving. |
| 60820.1 | 2026-08-20 | [run 32371130795](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32371130795) | Versions become date-anchored `<day>.<n>` (#1100). The engine and every pack restart from one day; every reader takes a legacy integer too, sorting below every date-anchored version, until #1106 removes the tolerance. |
| 60822.1 | 2026-08-23 | [run 32608725317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32608725317) | A pack manifest stops restating its own tree (#1246). `id`, `prose`, `badge`, `skills`, `worldRules` and `workRules` are resolved from the pack directory, an absent `detect`/`marker` means no fingerprint, and a `pack.mjs` declaration overrides only where a pack genuinely differs. Every pack version is gated behind this release — a manifest with no `id` is dropped outright by an older loader, which fails the mount self-test and stops that member converging at all. |
| 60823.1 | 2026-08-23 | [run 32609851921](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32609851921) | The member declaration is renamed `.claudinite-settings.json` and reshaped (#1252): each pack's installed version moves onto that pack's own entry, `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level, the `claudinite` and `maintenance` blocks are retired, and `taskScheduler.endpoints` becomes `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`. change against the trees it had before two rebases; this one is the tree that actually
ships. What it qualifies specifically is the settings-file rename: the canary held a
declaration spelled the old way when the run began, and the converged tree passed its

landing and its own converge.

Version 3's was dispatched against `9f5162a` — this change's tree, with only the
row you are reading edited after it — and it is the first rehearsal in weeks that
actually rehearsed anything. The gate had been driving the canary's
vendored BASELINING worker, which stood down and exited 0 the moment the canary

now fails unless the run says in words that it converged.

Version 4's was dispatched against `e416aed1` — this change's tree, with only the
run id in the row you are reading edited after it.

Version 60820.1's was dispatched against `1f05d43` — this change's tree. Two edits
landed after it: the row you are reading, and an issue number corrected in a comment
in `version.mjs`, neither of which any code reads.

Version 5's was dispatched against `93ca7bd` — this change's tree, with only the
run id in the row you are reading edited after it. It converged the canary through
BOTH flows (`update: engine`, then `update: packs`) and the converged tree passed
its self-test, which is what qualifies the rename specifically: the canary held a
declaration and a mount spelled the old way when the run began, and the packs
loaded anyway.

Version 60822.1's was dispatched against `a5eaeaf` — this change's tree rebased onto
the main it merges into, with only the row you are reading edited after it. Two
earlier rehearsals qualified earlier bases and are superseded by this one, which
qualifies the released tree: the canary converged both flows against a canon whose

loaded them and passed its self-test.

I can't. You've found a real hole in my plan.

`create-work-item <pack>/<task>` resolves against tasks that already exist — `no task "<target>" in this repo's declared packs` — and runs *that task's* declared `code_work`. There's no mechanism to attach custom code to an item. `--context` lines are just text, and text only reaches the **agentic** phase.

And the agentic phase can't see the bag either. Code-work is a subprocess of the executor's Actions job, so it inherits `taskEnv`. The agent session is fired over HTTP to the CCR routine endpoint and runs elsewhere — `CLAUDINITE_VARS` never reaches it. So "an ad-hoc item that reports its environment" is precisely the thing the architecture forbids: the phase that can see the bag can't be customised, and the phase that can be customised can't see it.

That also means the Shepherd item I cited as precedent — *"Ad-hoc: report the run's environment variables"* — cannot have observed the executor's real env. I used it as evidence without checking what it actually did.

input.body:
#1511 re-opened the withhold lane in code. It did not update the two documents that tell the apply-stage session what to do with a staged workflow file — both still state the lane is retired. The brief now says two opposite things, and the fleet resolved it both ways.

## What the brief says

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md`, intro:

> **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; **you are the credential.**

Same file, §2:

> Nothing withholds a workflow file any more … So: **never move a file into `.github/workflows/`** … If the branch still carries staged files after the flow ran, that is a canon bug — park it (§5).

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §18 agrees with §2:

> Consequently **no update flow touches `.github/workflows/`**, and the `pending-workflows/` withhold lane does not exist.

## What the fleet did with it

All 13 members converged at ~12:09 on 2026-08-31, each staging one withheld executor workflow and raising an apply stage. The sessions then split.

**Delivered (8)** — missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite#392:

> Applied the withheld executor workflow file to .github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml (Actions token cannot write there), removed the staging file … delivered PR #393 (squash-merged as cfab500).

**Parked (5)** — missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#309:

> `.claudinite/pending-workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` is still staged on that branch, which task.md §2 identifies as a canon bug: no flow should compute or stage a workflow file into that lane any more (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §18) — the lane is retired. Not moving it into `.github/workflows/`, not treating it as deliverable content. … Leaving PR #310 open pending a human call.

Both sessions read the same brief and reasoned correctly from different halves of it. ClaudiniteCanary, LaughCounter, TLDR, VascularColoring and hitbut sit at `task:status:needs-human-decision` with their update PRs open and the staged file undelivered.

## Why this is the defect and not the sessions

A brief that supports two opposite actions has no correct reading, so which one a session takes is not something any amount of care on its part can fix. The 8/5 split is the measurement of that: same input, same instructions, both outcomes. Every apply stage carrying a withheld workflow is exposed to it until the contradiction is removed.

The rule this broke is the canon's own: *an owner reversing a standing decision — purge every place in the repo that still states the old decision (docs, comments, code defaults) and record the new one where a future session reads it.* #1511 changed the code and the module comments and stopped there. `task.md` is not documentation about the mechanism, it is the mechanism's instruction to the agent, and it is the one place that decides what actually happens.

## Fix

1. `task.md` §2 becomes the delivery instruction: a staged file under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` is expected, and moving it into `.github/workflows/` is the session's job — it holds the credential the Action token lacks.
2. `DESIGN.md` §18 states the re-opened lane instead of its absence.
3. Bump `claudinite-lifecycle`; `task.md` is pack content and reaches members on the converge.
4. Re-run the five parked members and confirm from their live workflow files.

Refs #1509, #1511, #1522, #1317
